original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: A source-bound finite certificate of eliminated scalar field-product terms with complete raw-pencil replay preserved; wall-time improvement remains inconclusive.
scope_change_reason: Two complete alternating measurements had lower medians but overlapping ranges. The deliverable therefore claims the exact arithmetic work removed, not a reliable wall-time speedup.
bottleneck_link: Reduce deterministic arithmetic work in exact pencil extraction used to screen two-slice tensor mechanisms. This does not certify a faster whole replay or physical supplier.
stop_rule: Stop after the first exact positive arithmetic reduction on the unchanged complete caller, with product preservation and source invalidation controls. Retain the inconclusive timing evidence without a speed claim.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the exact work reduction give a reliable wall-time gain on a quiescent host?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Python overhead and host variation can consume a scalar-arithmetic saving.
open_questions.first_step: Run the same complete five-pair benchmark on a controlled host, retain all samples and verify the full output hash.

open_questions.question: Can the product kernel benefit the separate raw-pencil SL transporter?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That caller uses extracted maps but may have different bottlenecks.
open_questions.first_step: Profile one complete raw-pencil-sl-transport phase and define its input/output and coverage boundary before installing this kernel.
open_questions.blocked_by: No transporter measurement or coverage argument is supplied.
